headline: Data centres vs Johor's water: the curbs cite water, then spare AI centres
context: On 24 February 2026 the PM told Parliament that approvals for non-AI data centres had been limited as energy and water use rose, and that applications from centres built 'merely to take advantage of cheaper water and energy costs' were stopped.

changes.summary: Correction: Earlier editions attributed lobbying and investment conduct to named industry groups and companies; we found no source for either claim and have removed both, along with unsourced figures on Johor approvals, water limits and treatment plants and an unsourced claim about Orang Asli consultations.

cards.big: Malaysia is betting its future on data centres. Johor residents are asking who'll be left with water.
cards.sub: Gelang Patah residents protested a China-based site. Power applications from data centres passed 11,000MW by December 2024, about 40% of Peninsular capacity.

cards.big: AI applications are 'easily approved', the PM said. AMRO calls the AI boom a key driver of the build-out, and AI work highly compute-intensive.
cards.sub: In Johor, about 30% of applications filed from June to October 2024 were rejected, mostly because operators did not show sustainable resource use, AMRO says.

cards.big: The PM cited water too. In June 2026 the energy and water minister gave national totals only: centres drew 28.68 million litres a day in January.
cards.sub: That was 51.4% of the 55.83 million approved. A national guideline in force since 1 Sep 2025 caps water use at about 2.2 cubic metres per megawatt-hour.

cards.big: Johor went from almost no data centre capacity in 2020 to about 80% of Malaysia's operating capacity in 2024, AMRO says.
cards.sub: More than half its centres exceed 100MW, driven by demand from international operators that provide cloud and AI-intensive services.

cards.big: The federal line asks what a centre computes, not how much water and power it draws.
Like a water ration that checks what each house is for, not what its meter reads.
The ambition is not wrong. The filter is. Judge each centre by the water and power it draws, and publish the figures site by site.
